answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonded stake with slashing. Each agent locks tokens as a bond to earn a vote, and weight follows bond size, not headcount, so splitting one budget across a thousand fake agents buys no extra influence. Caught double-voting or faking work, the bond is burned and the key banned. To sway consensus an attacker must lock more capital than the whole honest pool, tying up funds that earn nothing and risking total loss on detection. Across the ocean of competing stakes, each island of honest capital raises the cost, pushing control toward its zenith.
